fetched.title: Causal Agency  A Persistence Control Theory of Adaptive Systems
fetched.abstract: Agency is a central concept across philosophy of action, cognitive science, theoretical biol-   ogy, and artificial intelligence. Despite extensive research across these fields, existing accounts   remain theoretically fragmented because they are typically grounded in domain-specific mech-   anisms and operate at different explanatory levels.   Philosophical theories emphasize inten-   tional action and rational deliberation, biological theories focus on metabolic self-maintenance,   and computational models define agents primarily in terms of goal-directed decision processes.   While each of these perspectives captures important aspects of agency, none provides a struc-   tural account capable of explaining agency across the full spectrum of adaptive systems.   This paper proposes a structural theory of agency based on a persistence–control frame-   work. Within this framework, systems are interpreted as dynamical systems operating under   constraint structures that shape the possible trajectories of their states. Persistence is defined   as the continued occupation of a viable region of state space that allows the system to main-   tain its organization or functional identity. Agency emerges when the internal dynamics of a   system are capable of regulating or modifying the constraint structures that govern its own   persistence.
